other.remelting: repeatedly flipped and remelted nine times

evidence.quote: The Ti66.8V11.2Al9.6Zr6.2Nb6.2 (at.%) LRCCA was prepared using a vacuum arc melting furnace under high-purity argon atmosphere. To ensure chemical homogeneity, the as-cast ingot was repeatedly flipped and remelted nine times.
Subsequently, the alloy ingot underwent homogenization treatment at 1000 ◦C for 2 h followed by water quenching.

The homogenized ingot was then subjected to multi-pass hot rolling at 800 ◦C, with each pass preceded by 10 min of reheating. The final thickness of the rolled sheet was approximately 1.6 mm, representing about 80 % thickness reduction. Immediately after achieving the target thickness, the hot-rolled sheet was water-quenched, with this state designated as HR.
Finally, the hot-rolled sheets were annealed at 580 ◦C and 740 ◦C for 0.5 h, respectively, followed by water quenching. These two states were labeled as HRA580 and HRA740 correspondingly.
